newsitem.title: USA: Candidates urged to sign no new tax pledge.
newsitem.headline: Candidates urged to sign no new tax pledge.

text.p: A group opposed to tax increases said Tuesday that 118 congressional candidates, almost all of them Republicans, had signed a pledge not to vote to raise taxes if elected.

Grover Norquist, president of Americans for Tax Reform, said at a news conference the list of incumbents and challengers included 108 House candidates and 10 running for the Senate. He said all were Republicans except Democratic Senate candidates in Kansas and Wyoming and a Democratic House candidate in Kansas.

Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole has made a 15 percent tax cut the centrepiece of his campaign. One of his economic advisers, former Reagan administration Budget Director James Miller, endorsed the no-new-tax pledge, which Dole has signed.
"As an adviser for the Dole-Kemp campaign, I want to tell you how important it is to keep taxes low and to cut taxes," Miller said.
Norquist said his group was non-partisan. But all the other speakers at the news conference criticised Democratic President Clinton for raising taxes in 1993.
"If Clinton gets re-elected, he's going to want to raise your payroll taxes," said David Keating, president of the National Taxpayers Union.
"Americans don't trust politicians not to raise taxes," added Brian Lopina of the Christian Coalition.
Norquist said a copy of the no-new-tax pledge would be sent by fax to the White House every hour Tuesday to give Clinton a chance to sign it.
